prompt: Create a high-fidelity desktop web application UI design comp for APIShield, a local Python API migration and AI repair tool. This is a designed application screen, flat front-facing screenshot, landscape 16:10, not a poster, not an angled device mockup. Exact product truth: synthetic shipping project, a POST endpoint moved from /labels to /labels/create; consuming function create_label in src/parcel.py; declared business rule Preserve package identity and exact integer grams; linked pytest test test_shipping_preserves_package_and_weight. One AI-generated repair passed one configured test and one linked business-rule test. Original code unchanged. Display compact badge 'Design concept' somewhere unobtrusive. Graph shows these existing relations only, not invented transitive dependencies or analytics. Beautiful professionally art-directed components, strong alignment, purposeful clear grouping, carefully placed buttons, precise icons, high-quality type, readable labels. Main navigation simple: Workspace, Runs, Settings; Help visible as a small affordance. Project selector 'Shipping API'. Persistent short sequence Check changes → Explore impact → Review repair. Always one clear primary action, 'Review repair'. Existing recorded report, not actively running, no fake percentage or inflated metrics. Code shows before /labels and after /labels/create, payload unchanged. Include a short contextual help sentence rather than paragraphs. Tight professional component proportions and deliberate visual hierarchy, no generic icon-card grid, no huge marketing headline, no gradients/glow, no decorative illustration, no graphs unrelated to the task. This is static design imagery; do not label animation as already implemented. Direction A: REVIEW STUDIO. A visually sophisticated light code-review workspace with pale cool grey canvas #eef0f2, white content panes, deep slate #223047 and confident cobalt #245be5. Modern finely tuned humanist sans, 28px title 'Review this API change', 14px UI labels, mono exclusively code. Composition: narrow 180px left navigation with elegant small logo; slim project/run header at top; contextual workflow strip below. Main body is a wide 60% impact graph pane left and 40% 'Repair ready' inspector right; selected node connects endpoint, function, rule and test via sparse crisp orthogonal links and semantic node chips with restrained amber, blue and green accents. Lower aligned 30% region contains a compact side-by-side code diff left and two test evidence rows right. Graph pane has compact toolbar, fit controls and a selected-state accent. The inspector includes a concise explanation, collected/passed evidence, and a beautifully placed solid cobalt Review repair button. Real measured whitespace; information doesn't drown in blank cards. All graph labels and component text crisp. Consistent 10px pane rounding, quiet directional shadows only where layers need separation. A beautiful finished SaaS workbench, not a plain settings dashboard.
note: Visual proposal only. Generated code, dates, avatars and evidence labels must be replaced with actual backend truth; no authentication or invented business-rule proof.
